sources.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Easy Training Data for Hard Tasks — quoted full-text passages (arXiv 2401.06751v2 PDF)

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The paper reports that when hard data costs twice as much to label as easy data, fitting on easy data more often than not gives higher hard-test accuracy. Under a noise assumption where hard data is mislabeled twice as often as easy data, easy data is preferable when its labeling error rate is 10% or higher (hard data 20% or higher).
title: Easy data can beat hard data when hard labels cost twice as much or are noisier
